brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Two-storey 3-cell base (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full at level 0 and same at level 1) with solid top covers (cover:0,0,1;full;top etc.) forming continuous deck f16 ~310x310mm, staged with book-stack prop; capped faces and locked joints.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: Configurator checks fit/collision only and parts are 3D-printed in user-chosen material. No load testing or certification is available, so a 50kg rating cannot be verified. Geometry provides a sturdy two-storey frame with joint bolts, but strength/material/heat/UV/waterproofing is outside this system – unmet by rule.
Two double-height notch drawer frames installed: notch:0#-1,1#notch0 and notch:0#1,-1#notch4 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf-x2), each providing a sliding compartment on level 0.

finish.summary: Built a compact 2-storey hexagonal shelf (3 bases per level, topped with 3 solid covers forming one deck) with two double-height notch drawers at ground level. Books staged on top shelf. 50kg load rating cannot be certified in this 3D-printed modular system – geometry is braced and bolted but no material/strength verification exists.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
